composers_checked.name: Cambini, Giuseppe Maria
composers_checked.note: Floor from Apple Music track lists (Stradivarius, Musica Novantiqua, Bella Musica, Tactus, Claves, Pan Classics, Toccata, Warner, Auvidis), MusicBrainz and RISM. Gap check against Wikipedia's work list (149 quartets, 110 Séguin quintets, 100+ trios), the Amadeus catalogue (Séguin quintets Nos. 1–86, Op. 2 trios, Op. 21 quartets), Trimpert numbers via RISM, and the recordings found: added the G minor quartet T. 116 and six Séguin quintets.

note: Cambini strings (c30). 1) Only works with a commercial recording are kept (decision 3, prolific minor composer): the six Lacépède quartets (T. 169–174, Stradivarius), the six Op. 21 quartets for violin, two violas and cello (Musica Novantiqua; No. 3 also Bella Musica), Op. 33 trios Nos. 3–5 (Tactus), Op. 40 No. 3, T. 159 (Claves), and as gap additions the G minor quartet T. 116 (Quartetto Italiano, Les Adieux, Cambini-Paris) and six of the 110 two-cello quintets written for Armand Séguin after 1794 (Library of Congress autographs, first printed by Amadeus; Nos. 1, 4, 23 Pan Classics; Nos. 13, 16, 47 Toccata Classics, October 2026). 2) Lacépède set: RISM's print record gives the keys in print order as E-flat, F, B minor, D, G minor, C. Stradivarius's metadata calls No. 1 'B-flat' and T. 173 'G major'; RISM (print title and a Torrefranca copy of No. 5's finale) has G minor, so G minor is used. IMSLP's typeset numbers the B minor quartet T. 169 and the E-flat T. 170, which conflicts with print order (T. 172–174 follow print order), so Nos. 1–3 carry no T. number. Year left blank: dedicated to 'Monsieur le Sénateur Lacépède' (senator from 1799), so not c. 1780 as IMSLP's print date says. 3) Op. 21: RISM ties Nos. 1–3 to T. 66–68 (B-flat, F, D); Trimpert's T. 69–71 (E-flat, A, B-flat) probably are Nos. 4–6, but the order is unconfirmed, so those three have no key in the title. 4) Not added for lack of identification: an F major quartet ('6 quatuors, No. 6') on the Les Adieux disc (Auvidis 1996), presumably the same book as T. 116 (perhaps T. 120); the Cambini quartet on Quatuor Joachim's 'Quatuors concertants: Cambini, Jadin, Boulogne, Gossec' (1996; AllMusic refused the fetch); and 'String Quintets Op. 13 Nos. 1–3' by the Serenissima Ensemble (self-released 2015; Amadeus prints Séguin quintets No. 73 in A minor and No. 75 in F as 'op. 13/1' and 'op. 13/3', keys of the recording unconfirmed). 5) For c31 (mixed): the Op. 26 trios are for flute, violin and viola (Trio Tourte, Tactus 2012; UT Orpheus edition 2022); Tactus also has oboe quartets with keyboard and Arte Sonora flute trios. 6) Levels: all 4 by analogy with Haydn's Op. 33 and Boccherini's Op. 11 No. 5 quintet; Cambini's quartets concertants pass the lead between parts, and his viola writing is busy. Popularity: all lesser-known.
